subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: What should the public web-tool egress boundary be for this request: web_fetch-local hostname allowlist, a broader managed-proxy policy, or a cross-tool search/fetch/browser policy?
rationale: This adds an operator-trusted security/config surface, and current related PRs encode different answers that automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve a scoped web_fetch allowlist first
options.body: Review and sponsor the narrow web_fetch hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step, while keeping deny/search/proxy coverage explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Make the managed proxy the boundary
options.body: Pause local web_fetch config work and route application-owned egress policy through the managed proxy direction instead.

options.title: Design a cross-tool policy
options.body: Require a broader design covering fetch, search, browser, provider fallback, redirects, caches, and plugin HTTP before implementation lands.

recommendation.title: Approve a scoped web_fetch allowlist first
recommendation.body: Review and sponsor the narrow web_fetch hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step, while keeping deny/search/proxy coverage explicit follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across the SSRF, guarded fetch, and web_fetch runtime surfaces involved in this boundary choice.
